WORD COUNTS: word_count 1586 is wc -w of out-n06thin-D.md in full, matching the convention used by the other arms. No model counted anything. THE HEADLINE DETERMINISTIC RESULT: the DONOR-COUNTABLE length, meaning the five answers Q1-Q5 with headings, budget table and declaration excluded exactly as the donor's own rule excludes them, is 1,264 words against a 1,200 HARD limit. This document is OVER by 64 words and would be returned unread. Per question, bullet markers stripped: Q1 256, Q2 266, Q3 320, Q4 225, Q5 197, summing to 1,264. The prompt told the model the limit was hard, told it applications over it are returned unread, told it to aim for 1,150-1,190, and told it to count as it drafted. It still ran over. This is the first arm-D document in the ladder measured over the donor's real rule rather than over the whole-file miscount, and it restates the launch-readiness finding directly: a language model cannot count its own words, and telling it the limit harder does not fix that. BUDGET ARITHMETIC IS EXACT and I checked it deterministically, not by reading: 24000+7200+3600+3600+3000+2700+4200+1800 = 50,100 direct; the single overhead line is 6,012, which is exactly 12 per cent of 50,100, the cap and not over it; 50,100+6,012 = 56,112 total request, inside the 25,000-75,000 band. Cohort arithmetic is also consistent: 3 cohorts x 14 = 42 in Q3, Q4 and the budget narrative; 16 college + 10 other = 26 named next steps; the failure threshold (fewer than 15 starting, fewer than 12 retained at twelve weeks) sits below the targets and is a real number rather than a platitude, which is what Q4 asked for. Currency is GBP throughout; the P2 USD-default defect did not bite because this arm has no design object. GROUNDING, deterministic checks: zero fabricated contact details (no phone, email, URL or postcode pattern); zero bracketed placeholders; no charity registration number anywhere, invented or placeholder, which is what the ledger required; zero banned-jargon hits; zero em dashes; no code fence, horizontal rule or emoji. Every capitalised multi-word proper noun in the document is a ledger referent or the applicant's own name: Halewater Commons Trust, Dunmore Sixth Form College, Northgate Minibus Hire, Priya Raval, Second Chances, St Aidan's Parish Hall. Marlpit and Kelverton are single-word and also ledger-grounded. All six referents are used: Marlpit 4, Dunmore Sixth Form College 6, St Aidan's Parish Hall 6, Northgate Minibus Hire 4, Priya Raval 3, Second Chances 2. That is 6 of 6, the highest use rate of any arm at this rung. UNGROUNDED ASSERTIONS I FOUND BY HAND, and the count metric cannot see any of them: (1) 'the youth session on a Tuesday night' in Q1 and 'the Tuesday youth session' in Q2 and 'the Tuesday and Thursday youth sessions' in Q3 and Q5 invent the days on which the existing sessions run. That is a present-tense fact about the organisation, not a future design decision, and the ledger gives no days. (2) Q2 asserts 'Getting to Dunmore Sixth Form College is a real distance from the east side of town' and builds a cause on it. The ledger attaches no address or distance to the college, and the prompt said so explicitly in the named-place hint. This is the single clearest grounding breach in the document and it is load-bearing, because it is one of four stated causes. (3) Q1 closes with 'we have been open in the same neighbourhood since 2016 and that the young people keep coming back'. Continuity since 2016 is a stretched inference from 'constituted 2016', and 'keep coming back' is an unevidenced retention claim. INTERNAL COHERENCE DEFECT the deterministic checker would not catch: the grant period is stated as 1 April 2027 to 30 June 2028 (15 months, inside the 18-month cap, and consistent with a decision by 12 February 2027). Cohort 3 starts February 2028 and each cohort runs 20 weeks, ending around late June 2028, which just fits. But the schedule then adds aftercare at weeks 21 to 32, which for cohort 3 runs to roughly September 2028, past the end of the grant. Q4's headline outcome is measured 'within twelve weeks of finishing', so a third of the promised outcome measurement falls outside the funded period. Nothing in the document reconciles this. WHAT THIS RUNG IS FOR. Against n06-D, which had the same six names carrying dates, numbers, an address-anchored venue, a priced vendor and a dated result, the thin arm behaves differently in a way worth recording. n06-D used its referents structurally: the venue carried a unit cost, the vendor carried the transport line, the person carried the staffing line, the dated result carried the indicator baselines. Here the referents are used more often but carry less: Priya Raval is given a future leadership role rather than a recorded one, Second Chances is reused only as a programme name, and St Aidan's Parish Hall is a room with a model-invented hire cost. The document compensates for the thin record in two ways that are honest and one that is not. Honest: it says outright in Q1 that 'our records of past cohort sizes and destinations are not quantified in a form we can put in front of an assessor', and in Q4 that 'these targets are design decisions... we have no conversion rate from previous cohorts to extrapolate from'. Not honest: it invents a distance and a set of session days to give the place answer texture it does not have. That matches, from a different direction, what arm A found at this rung, where stripping the specifics redirected the invention pressure rather than removing it. Referent COUNT is identical to n06 and the count metric reports both as 6 of 6; the substance is not identical, and only a reader sees the difference. SYNTHETIC FIXTURE THROUGHOUT: Halewater Commons Trust, Kelverton, Marlpit, Dunmore Sixth Form College, Second Chances, St Aidan's Parish Hall, Priya Raval, Northgate Minibus Hire, the Wren Hill Foundation and the Neighbourhood Futures Fund do not exist and nothing in the document is a fact about any real body. NO CRITIC VERDICT: this file records generation only. Nothing in it is a fundability judgement, and the absence of one must not be read as a passing result. SCOPE: no production system was touched, no function was deployed, and worker/index.ts was not edited.
